exposure: Mode of delivery (Caesarean section vs Vaginal delivery)
outcome: General cognitive ability at around age 18, measured using a normalized general cognitive test battery
cohort: 579,244 singleton males born in Sweden between 1973 and 1987 who conscripted before 2006
finding: The study found a weak association between caesarean section birth and lower general cognitive ability in young adult males, but this association was largely explained by familial factors.
mod_finding: Both elective and non-elective cesarean sections were associated with lower general cognitive ability scores compared to vaginal delivery, but these associations were attenuated in sibling analyses.
